text: The report compares 3,110 ENIGMA Genome Depot cultured-isolate genomes, primarily isolated from the Oak Ridge Field Research Center over 20+ years of cultivation, with 2,279 QC-passing subsurface metagenome-assembled genomes from kbase_ke_pangenome collected from groundwater, aquifer, and subsurface samples globally.
quote: This report compares two genome cohorts and quantifies the per-function bias between them: (i) the **ENIGMA Genome Depot cultured isolates** (3,110 genomes, primarily isolated from the Oak Ridge Field Research Center over 20+ years of cultivation), and (ii) **subsurface MAGs from `kbase_ke_pangenome`** (2,279 QC-passing metagenome-assembled genomes from groundwater, aquifer, and subsurface samples globally).
heading: Scope

text: The report pivoted from 623 ORFRC-specific MAGs in enigma_coral because their assembly FASTAs at /h/jmc/data/ were inaccessible from JupyterHub, so its findings concern subsurface systems generally rather than Oak Ridge specifically.
quote: The MAG side was originally scoped to 623 ORFRC-specific MAGs from `enigma_coral`, but the underlying assembly FASTAs at `/h/jmc/data/` are not accessible from JupyterHub (see `RESEARCH_PLAN.md` v2); the pivot to the pangenome's pre-annotated pan-subsurface MAGs broadens the question from "what does cultivation miss at Oak Ridge specifically?" to "what does cultivation miss in subsurface systems generally?".
heading: Scope

text: The report's MAG cohort uses global kbase_ke_pangenome subsurface/groundwater MAGs rather than ORFRC wells because CORAL assembly FASTAs were inaccessible, so its results do not directly measure the Oak Ridge cultivation gap.
quote: Due to inaccessibility of CORAL assembly FASTAs, the MAG cohort was drawn from `kbase_ke_pangenome` subsurface/groundwater MAGs globally rather than from ORFRC wells specifically. This broadens the comparison from site-specific to a general subsurface cultivation bias, which is arguably more generalizable but means the results do not directly measure the cultivation gap at Oak Ridge specifically.

text: The report's QC-filtered MAG cohort has mean completeness 78.7%, and some KOs scored absent may lie in the missing 20% of the genome.
quote: MAGs are inherently less complete than isolate genomes (mean completeness 78.7% in our QC-filtered cohort). Some KOs scored as "absent from MAGs" may simply be in the missing 20% of the genome.
heading: Limitations

text: MAG incompleteness makes the 813 MAG-enriched KOs a conservative estimate whose true count is likely higher, while some cultured-enriched KOs may be false positives.
quote: This would make the 813 "MAG-enriched" KOs a conservative estimate (true count is likely higher) but also means some cultured-enriched KOs may be false positives.
heading: Limitations

text: The report identifies the 4-fold genome size difference (5.8 vs 1.5 Mbp) between cultured and MAG cohorts as the dominant driver of the bias distribution.
quote: The 4-fold genome size difference (5.8 vs 1.5 Mbp) between cohorts is the dominant driver of the bias distribution.
heading: Limitations

text: The report did not perform genome-size-normalized analysis to isolate cultivation selection from genome streamlining.
quote: A genome-size-normalized analysis (e.g., comparing only KOs within size-matched phyla) would isolate cultivation selection from genome streamlining, but was not performed in this analysis.
heading: Limitations

text: Cultured genome KOs were annotated by the ENIGMA Genome Depot pipeline with unknown tool version, whereas MAG KOs came from bakta through kbase_ke_pangenome.bakta_db_xrefs.
quote: Cultured genomes were annotated via the ENIGMA Genome Depot pipeline (unknown annotation tool version), while MAG KOs were derived from bakta via `kbase_ke_pangenome.bakta_db_xrefs`.
heading: Limitations

text: Systematic annotation-pipeline sensitivity differences could bias the cultured–MAG comparison, although the report considers KO-level comparison more robust than pathway-level comparison.
quote: Systematic sensitivity differences between annotation pipelines could introduce bias, though KO-level comparison is more robust than pathway-level.
heading: Limitations

text: The cultured collection spans 20+ years of ENIGMA isolation primarily at ORFRC, while MAGs span global subsurface sites, so composition differences may reflect geography as much as cultivation bias.
quote: The cultured collection spans 20+ years of ENIGMA isolation efforts primarily at ORFRC. The MAG cohort spans multiple subsurface sites globally. Community composition differences may reflect geographic variation as much as cultivation bias.
